summary: Source-anchored research for Diagnostic Tool Design. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Offline analysis is one way to avoid issuing additional database commands during diagnosis: the mdbkit repository describes analysis commands that read supplied files without a database connection and print proposed actions for human review. This is a documented architectural example, not an independent audit of the implementation or a claim that every diagnostic task can be completed offline. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Production diagnostic collectors should expose scope and deadline controls. Percona mongodb_exporter documents collection allowlists, a collection-count threshold that disables selected collectors, and a timeout offset; it warns that free-space statistics can cause delays with many collections or indexes. This supports bounding collection work, without proving that every diagnostic command is lock-free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The mdiag _redactfile function matches a finite list of configuration secret names, substitutes a redacted marker, and includes a SHA-256 digest when available. This is targeted redaction, not evidence of general query-document PII coverage. OWASP recommends removing or protecting sensitive log data through several possible methods; it does not mandate regex redaction as the sole compliant design. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

MongoDB ftdc NewStreamingCollector bounds retained batches by sample count: Add flushes when count reaches maxSamples, and FlushCollector resolves the payload, writes it, and resets the collector. This is a collection-side sample limit; the implementation does not establish a strict byte-buffer cap for a streaming BSON parser or prove prevention of replica-node OOM kills. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A diagnostic bundle needs redaction coverage appropriate to its contents. The mdiag _redactfile implementation matches an explicit list of configuration-secret keys, while independent diagnosis-data research explains that rule and regex approaches can both miss sensitive data and remove useful evidence. Inference: the presence of a regex redactor alone cannot establish complete PII protection. (medium confidence)

Query shapes can group similar queries without distinguishing every literal value: MongoDB examples use different date constants with the same shape hashes. Namespace and field-name protection is a separate concern: $queryStats offers transformIdentifiers for hashing those identifiers. Inference: shape-based grouping should not be presented as complete anonymization or as proof of deterministic error grouping. (medium confidence)

MongoDB documents query shapes as a way to group similar queries, including examples where different date constants yield the same shape hash. This supports grouping query workloads, but not guaranteed deterministic error grouping or anonymization: Atlas explicitly warns that shapes retaining field names can contain PII even when values are redacted. (medium confidence)

serverStatus exposes separate lock-wait counters and election-reason counters, including elections after a member cannot reach its primary within electionTimeoutMillis. These counters can inform a diagnostic tool's evidence model; the command reference does not establish that a scraper timeout held a database lock and caused an election, or that a small serverStatus timeout fixes that sequence. (low confidence)

Collector scope is a concrete overhead control: Percona's exporter reference provides collection filters and a collection-count cutoff for selected collectors, and warns that free-space statistics can delay processing with many collections or indexes. PMM documentation likewise warns that high collection limits can increase CPU and memory use. Design inference: expose selective collection rather than assuming all diagnostic commands are cheap. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The inspected implementations distinguish retention control from input validation: MongoDB's streaming collector flushes and resets after a sample-count threshold, while js-bson checks declared document lengths against the supplied buffer and checks document termination. These passages support testing both controls separately; they do not establish a strict parser byte cap or prove prevention of replica-node OOM kills. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
